title: A part sale invoiced with Unassigned is credited to Unassigned
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • You are signed in as a user with the "Admin" role at {Location-A}.
    For example: {Location-A} is Staging Heavy Duty - 9919.
  • Two active staff members at {Location-A} have their "Sales Representative" switch on: {Sales-rep-A} and {Sales-rep-B}.
    For example: {Sales-rep-A} is ZZAUTOTEST Ann Able and {Sales-rep-B} is ZZAUTOTEST Ben Able.
  • Customer {Customer-A} shows "Sales Representative - Service Labor" {Sales-rep-A}, "Sales Representative - Service Parts" {Sales-rep-B} and "Sales Representative - Part Sales" reading "Unassigned".
    For example: {Customer-A} is ZZAUTOTEST SSR Fleet.
  • Part sale {Part-sale-1} for {Customer-A} started with Sales Representative "Unassigned", has one part, and was invoiced today without a representative being picked.
    For example: {Part-sale-1} is P-30001.
  • Starting screen: Reports > Sales By Representative is open for today in a desktop browser at least 1024 px wide, with Show Unassigned on and the Sales Type column turned on.
  • If any record above is missing, mark this test Blocked: "setup not done".
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 1: the whole of {Part-sale-1} is credited to Unassigned, as one "Part Sales" row; {Sales-rep-A} and {Sales-rep-B} are not credited with it.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Splitting Sales Representatives", Confluence 919928833, version 11 (21 Oct 2026, Chris Ward), read 22 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-10890, story SV-11268 (Story 4, Give a customer default representatives), story SV-11269 (Story 5, Credit each side on the invoice and in Sales By Representative)

  • S4-R18: “A part sale invoiced with no representative is credited, for the whole sale, to the person new part sales get from the customer (S4-R26), or to nobody when the Part Sales field reads "Unassigned".”
  • S5-R9: “A part sale is one "Part Sales" row holding every dollar of the invoice.”
